openItems.explanation: The October 15 payment of $1,324.70 (EFT 270988315406) went to tax period 12/2026, the calendar-year habit; HANGS's tax year ends June 30, so FY2027 is 06/2027. Until it is moved, the 1st installment is $1,324.70 short: $6.10 of penalty to November 8, $15.50 by December 15, and the December payment would go first to the 1st installment. A person (the controller, or with Form 2848 on file) asks the IRS to move it to 06/2027 as of October 15.

HANGS is a large corporation for FY2027 because FY2024 taxable income was $1,182,400.00, from the controller's summary, figured without NOL carryovers. A person confirms it against the FY2024 return as filed. The rule costs HANGS the prior-year base after the 1st installment: the regular 2nd installment recaptures $14,609.23 ($32,381.15 in all). The annualized method brings it to $18,308.87; paying $3,162.70 again, as the controller asks, would leave $15,146.17 short.

The annualized method rests on $255,613.93 for July to September 2026 (book income of $205,803.93 from the reviewed, not audited, quarterly figures, plus the tax adjustments) and on projected figures for 6 and 9 months ($704,263.93, $1,104,823.93). The NOL deduction is taken after annualizing, at 80% of the annualized income, as an extraordinary item on line 23b; a person confirms that treatment under Regulations section 1.6655-2(f). Refresh the 3rd and 4th installments when the six and nine months close. Form 2220 with Schedule A goes with the FY2027 return.

The $1,838.00 counts toward the 1st installment only when the FY2026 return is filed electing it on line 37a. That return is a draft, extended to April 15, 2027, with open items of its own (the excavator's special allowance, the officer pay resolution, the related-party contract). If its tax changes, so do the $12,650.79 base of the 1st installment and the credit. The date the credit counts from is not stated in the saved sources; the plan treats it as paid October 15, 2026. A person confirms both.

Unsigned plan. Nothing has been paid or scheduled: $18,308.87 on December 15, 2026, about $22,897.06 on March 15, 2027 and about $17,501.36 on June 15, 2027, all EFTPS, Form 1120, tax period 06/2027, estimated tax. Paying the annualized amounts leaves about $9,217.70 due October 15, 2027 on the projected tax of $71,087.69; the board may prefer the regular amounts for cash planning. The projection changes as each quarter closes.

rules.question: Is HANGS a large corporation for FY2027?
rules.whyItMatters: A large corporation may use last year's tax for its 1st installment only. The test is $1,000,000 of taxable income, figured without NOL carryovers, in any of the three tax years before.
rules.effective: 26 U.S.C. 6655(g)(2), as published by Cornell Law School's Legal Information Institute.
rules.excerpt: The term "large corporation" means any corporation if such corporation (or any predecessor corporation) had taxable income of $1,000,000 or more for any taxable year during the testing period. ... The term "testing period" means the 3 taxable years immediately preceding the taxable year involved. ... taxable income shall be determined without regard to any amount carried to the taxable year under section 172 or 1212(a). ... the $1,000,000 amount ... shall be divided among such members [of a controlled group].
matchPhrases: if such corporation (or any predecessor corporation) had taxable income of $1,000,000 or more for any taxable year during the testing period
means the 3 taxable years immediately preceding the taxable year involved
taxable income shall be determined without regard to any amount carried to the taxable year under section 172 or 1212(a)
the $1,000,000 amount specified in subparagraph (a) shall be divided among such members
rules.ruleOrLimit: Large corporation: $1,000,000 or more of taxable income, before NOL and capital loss carryovers, in any of the 3 preceding tax years; a controlled group shares the $1,000,000.
rules.hangsApplication: FY2026 $301,209.35 before the NOL deduction, FY2025 a loss of $2,904,180.00, FY2024 $1,182,400.00 with no carryover deducted. FY2024 is $1,000,000 or more, so HANGS is a large corporation for FY2027. No controlled group: Juniper Ridge Partners LLC, a customer, is a single-member LLC owned by Riley Tanaka, and HANGS owns no interest in it.
hangsFactsUsed: Estimated tax details for FY2027 (controlled group)

rules.question: What can a large corporation do with last year's tax?
rules.whyItMatters: It may base the 1st installment on last year's tax, and the 2nd installment must recapture whatever that saved.
rules.excerpt: Large corporations required to pay 100 percent of current year tax ... clause (ii) of paragraph (1)(B) shall not apply in the case of a large corporation. ... Subparagraph (A) shall not apply for purposes of determining the amount of the 1st required installment for any taxable year. Any reduction in such 1st installment by reason of the preceding sentence shall be recaptured by increasing the amount of the next required installment determined under paragraph (1) by the amount of such reduction.
matchPhrases: large corporations required to pay 100 percent of current year tax
clause (ii) of paragraph (1)(b) shall not apply in the case of a large corporation
subparagraph (a) shall not apply for purposes of determining the amount of the 1st required installment for any taxable year
shall be recaptured by increasing the amount of the next required installment determined under paragraph (1) by the amount of such reduction
rules.ruleOrLimit: Large corporation: 1st installment may be 25% of last year's tax; the 2nd recaptures the difference; the rest are 25% of this year's tax.
rules.hangsApplication: 1st installment 25% of $12,650.79 = $3,162.70. The regular 2nd installment is $17,771.92 (25% of the projected $71,087.69) plus the $14,609.23 recapture: $32,381.15. The 3rd and 4th are $17,771.92 each.

rules.question: How does Form 2220 set a large corporation's regular installments, and what counts as taxable income for the test?
rules.whyItMatters: Line 10 (and Schedule A line 35) give the large-corporation amounts: 25% of last year's tax in column (a), the recapture in column (b).
rules.taxYear: 2025 instructions, the latest published; the rules come from section 6655
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 2220 (2025), Part II line 8 and Part III line 10.
rules.excerpt: However, a large corporation can base only its first required installment on the prior year's tax. ... Taxable income, for this purpose, is modified to exclude net operating loss and capital loss carrybacks and carryovers. ... enter 25% of line 4 in column (a) of line 10. In column (b), figure the amount to enter as follows: Subtract line 4 from line 3, Add the result to the amount on line 3, and Multiply the total ... by 25% ... In columns (c) and (d), enter 25% of line 3. If the box on line 8 and the box on line 6 and/or line 7 are checked, follow the instructions ... (substituting "Schedule A, line 35" for "line 10" in the calculation).

rules.question: What is the required annual payment, and when does last year's tax count?
rules.whyItMatters: Each installment is 25% of the lesser of this year's tax or last year's tax, if last year was a full 12-month year with tax on the return; for a large corporation, last year's tax counts for the 1st installment only.
rules.excerpt: Except as otherwise provided in this section, the amount of any required installment shall be 25 percent of the required annual payment. ... the lesser of (i) 100 percent of the tax shown on the return for the taxable year ..., or (ii) 100 percent of the tax shown on the return of the corporation for the preceding taxable year. Clause (ii) shall not apply if the preceding taxable year was not a taxable year of 12 months, or the corporation did not file a return for such preceding taxable year showing a liability for tax.
matchPhrases: the amount of any required installment shall be 25 percent of the required annual payment
100 percent of the tax shown on the return of the corporation for the preceding taxable year
clause (ii) shall not apply if the preceding taxable year was not a taxable year of 12 months, or the corporation did not file a return for such preceding taxable year showing a liability for tax
rules.ruleOrLimit: Required annual payment: the lesser of 100% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's (a 12-month year, a return showing tax); each installment 25% of it.
rules.hangsApplication: FY2026 was 12 months with $12,650.79 of tax on the draft return; the return must be filed showing that tax for it to count. Projected FY2027 tax $71,087.69. As a large corporation HANGS uses $12,650.79 only for the 1st installment.
rules.unresolved: CREDIT-01: the FY2026 return is still a draft; its tax sets the 1st installment's base only once it is filed showing that tax.

rules.question: When are a June 30 year-end corporation's installments due?
rules.whyItMatters: The four due dates set the penalty clock: the 15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th and 12th months of the tax year.
rules.effective: Publication 542, Corporations, Estimated tax.
rules.excerpt: Installment payments are due by the 15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months of the corporation's tax year. ... Example 2. Your corporation's tax year ends June 30. Installment payments are due on October 15, December 15, March 15, and June 15. If any due date falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, the installment is due on the next business day. ... Also, if the corporation is a large corporation, it can use Method 2 to figure the first installment only.

if any due date falls on a saturday, sunday, or legal holiday, the installment is due on the next business day

include any overpayment from the corporation's 2024 tax return that was credited to the corporation's 2025 estimated tax
rules.ruleOrLimit: An overpayment credited from last year's return counts as an estimated tax payment.

rules.question: What must go with the FY2027 return, and what if an installment turns out short?
rules.whyItMatters: Using the annualized method, or a large corporation basing its 1st installment on last year's tax, means attaching Form 2220 even if no penalty is due.
rules.effective: Publication 542, Estimated tax: Refiguring required installments; Form 2220.
rules.excerpt: An immediate catch-up payment should be made to reduce any penalty resulting from the underpayment of any earlier installments. ... even if the corporation does not owe a penalty, complete and attach the form to the corporation's tax return if any of the following apply. The annualized income installment method was used to figure any required installment. ... The corporation is a large corporation figuring its first required installment based on the prior year's tax.
matchPhrases: an immediate catch-up payment should be made to reduce any penalty resulting from the underpayment of any earlier installments
complete and attach the form to the corporation's tax return if any of the following apply
the annualized income installment method was used to figure any required installment
the corporation is a large corporation figuring its first required installment based on the prior year's tax
rules.pageOrSection: Estimated tax: Refiguring required installments; Underpayment penalty; Form 2220
rules.ruleOrLimit: Attach Form 2220 whenever the annualized method sets an installment or a large corporation uses last year's tax for the 1st; catch up at once on a short installment.
rules.hangsApplication: Both apply: Form 2220 with Schedule A goes with the FY2027 return. If the six- or nine-month actuals run ahead of the projection, the next payment catches up.

rules.question: Which installment does a payment go to, and how long does a short installment draw the penalty?
rules.whyItMatters: A payment always goes to the earliest unpaid installment, and each shortfall runs until paid, at the latest the 15th day of the 4th month after the year ends.
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 2220 (2025), Part IV.
rules.excerpt: The period of underpayment generally runs from the installment due date to the earlier of the date the underpayment is actually paid or the 15th day of the 4th month after the close of the tax year. ... A payment of estimated tax is applied against unpaid required installments in the order in which installments are required to be paid, regardless of the installment to which the payment pertains. ... The penalty is figured separately for each installment due date.
matchPhrases: the period of underpayment generally runs from the installment due date to the earlier of the date the underpayment is actually paid or the 15th day of the 4th month after the close of the tax year
a payment of estimated tax is applied against unpaid required installments in the order in which installments are required to be paid, regardless of the installment to which the payment pertains
the penalty is figured separately for each installment due date
rules.pageOrSection: Part IV, Figuring the Penalty; Who Must Pay the Underpayment Penalty
rules.ruleOrLimit: Payments go to the earliest unpaid installment; each shortfall draws the underpayment rate from its due date until paid, at most to October 15, 2027 for FY2027.
rules.hangsApplication: The $1,838.00 credit and the $1,324.70 paid October 15 together cover the 1st installment, $3,162.70, if both count. Nothing else is due before December 15.
rules.unresolved: EFTPS-01: the October 15 payment counts only once the IRS moves it from tax period 12/2026 to 06/2027.

rules.question: What underpayment rates apply from October 2025 through 2026?
rules.whyItMatters: The penalty is interest-like: the quarterly underpayment rate times the shortfall for each day it is unpaid. The FY2026 penalty ran at these rates; the FY2027 preview uses the fourth quarter of 2026.
rules.effective: IRS quarterly interest rates tables, 2025 and 2026.
rules.excerpt: 2026 interest rates by category ... 4th quarter (Oct-Dec) 3rd quarter (Jul-Sep) 2nd quarter (Apr-Jun) 1st quarter (Jan-Mar) ... Underpayment (corporate and non-corporate) 7% 7% 6% 7% ... 2025 interest rates by category ... Underpayment (corporate and non-corporate) 7% 7% 7% 7%

underpayment (corporate and non-corporate) 7% 7% 6% 7%
2025 interest rates by category
underpayment (corporate and non-corporate) 7% 7% 7% 7%
rules.ruleOrLimit: Underpayment rate: 7% October to December 2025, 7% January to March 2026, 6% April to June 2026, 7% July to September 2026, 7% October to December 2026.
rules.hangsApplication: A shortfall on the 1st FY2027 installment would run at 7% from October 15, 2026: $0.25 a day on $1,324.70. The rates for 2027 are not yet announced.
rules.unresolved: The rates from January 1, 2027 are not yet announced; the preview stops at December 31, 2026 or states a daily amount.

rules.question: Which FY2026 return sets the 1st installment's base if the draft changes?
rules.whyItMatters: The FY2026 return is still a draft; an amended return counts for an installment only if filed before that installment's due date.
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 2220 (2025), Who Must Pay the Underpayment Penalty.
rules.excerpt: In these instructions, "return" generally refers to the corporation's original return. However, an amended return is considered the original return if the amended return is filed by the due date (including extensions) of the original return. Also, for purposes of determining a required installment ..., if an amended return is filed for the prior tax year, then the return for the "prior tax year" includes the amended return, but only if the amended return is filed before the applicable installment due date.
matchPhrases: an amended return is considered the original return if the amended return is filed by the due date (including extensions) of the original return
then the return for the "prior tax year" includes the amended return, but only if the amended return is filed before the applicable installment due date
rules.pageOrSection: Who Must Pay the Underpayment Penalty
rules.ruleOrLimit: The prior-year tax is the tax on the FY2026 return as filed (an amendment by the extended due date counts as the original).
rules.hangsApplication: The FY2026 return, extended to April 15, 2027, shows $12,650.79 of tax in draft. Its open items (the excavator's special allowance, the officer pay resolution, the related-party contract) could change the tax, and with it the 1st installment's base and the $1,838.00 credit.
rules.unresolved: CREDIT-01: a person confirms the FY2026 tax when the return is finalized.

rules.question: When are the FY2026 and FY2027 returns due, with extensions?
rules.whyItMatters: A June 30 year beginning before 2026 files by the 15th day of the 3rd month with a 7-month extension; from tax years beginning in 2026 the usual 4th month and 6-month extension apply. The FY2027 due date also ends any penalty period.
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 7004, Maximum extension period.
rules.excerpt: The automatic extension period for time to file is generally 6 months. Exceptions apply for certain filers of Form 1041 and for C corporations with tax years ending June 30. ... C corporations with tax years ending June 30 and beginning before January 1, 2026, are eligible for an automatic 7-month extension of time to file ... For tax years beginning in 2026, the automatic extension period is 6 months.
matchPhrases: the automatic extension period for time to file is generally 6 months
c corporations with tax years ending june 30 and beginning before january 1, 2026, are eligible for an automatic 7-month extension of time to file
for tax years beginning in 2026, the automatic extension period is 6 months
rules.ruleOrLimit: FY2026 (began July 1, 2025): due September 15, 2026, extended 7 months to April 15, 2027. FY2027 (begins July 1, 2026): due October 15, 2027, 6-month extension.
rules.hangsApplication: The FY2026 return is extended to April 15, 2027. The FY2027 return is due Friday, October 15, 2027, when about $9,217.70 of tax remains due under this plan.

rules.question: How and by when must the remaining payments be made?
rules.whyItMatters: Corporate tax deposits must go by electronic funds transfer; a same-day EFTPS payment of $1 million or less must be in before 3 p.m. Eastern on a business day.
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 1120 (2025), Depository Method of Tax Payment.
rules.excerpt: Corporations must use electronic funds transfer (EFT) to make all federal tax deposits (such as deposits of employment, excise, and corporate income tax). ... EFTPS accepts same day payments of $1 million or less if the payment is submitted before 3:00 p.m. Eastern time on a business day.

eftps accepts same day payments of $1 million or less if the payment is submitted before 3:00 p.m. eastern time on a business day
rules.pageOrSection: Depository Method of Tax Payment: Electronic Deposit Requirement; Depositing on Time
rules.ruleOrLimit: EFT only; EFTPS same-day payments of $1 million or less before 3:00 p.m. Eastern on a business day.

rules.question: Can the estimated tax penalty be removed for reasonable cause?
rules.whyItMatters: If it cannot, the only way to avoid it is to pay the right amount, to the right tax period, on time.
rules.effective: IRS page on penalty relief for reasonable cause.
rules.excerpt: Reasonable cause is determined on a case-by-case basis considering all the facts and circumstances of your situation. ... Reasonable cause doesn't apply to certain penalties such as the estimated tax penalty.

reasonable cause doesn't apply to certain penalties such as the estimated tax penalty
rules.ruleOrLimit: Reasonable cause relief does not apply to the estimated tax penalty.
